passages.provision_quote: For personal property that is initially classified during or after tax year 2022 as class one, paragraph 8, 9, 10 or 13 pursuant to section 42-12001 personal property that is initially classified during or after tax year 2022 as class two (P) pursuant to section 42-12002 and personal property that is acquired during or after tax year 2022 and initially classified during or after tax year 2022 as class six pursuant to section 42-12006, paragraph 2 or 3, the assessor shall use a valuation factor of two and one-half percent.
passages.note: Enacted text of his prime-sponsored bill: a uniform change to how all class one, two (P) and six business personal property is valued, not a company-specific incentive.

rows.reasoning: The only record on file is HB 2822 (2022), which Weninger prime-sponsored and voted Y on: it sets "a valuation factor of two and one-half percent" for business personal property first classified in or after tax year 2022. That is a uniform change to how all such property is valued, applying to every business rather than to a recruited employer, so it does not speak to whether to "Offer incentives to attract businesses" or to "Don't give companies tax breaks or subsidies"; the annex puts a change to how all business property is valued at adjacent. No passage survives V2, so nothing can seat a rung.
